themes_detail.label: Hazardous Materials Spike
themes_detail.summary: Hazardous materials complaints exploded to 5 incidents 3 weeks ago, a 1233% spike above the 0.4 weekly average, suggesting a localized contamination or disposal problem that has not yet resolved in CD 411.
evidence: 5 hazardous materials complaints filed 3 weeks ago vs. 0.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (1233% increase)
Z-score of 9.55 indicates extreme statistical anomaly
No follow-up context available on source or resolution status
reporting_angles: What specific hazardous material was reported and where in Bayside/Douglaston/Little Neck?
Has the source been identified and remediated, or are residents still at risk?

themes_detail.label: Indoor Air Quality Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Indoor air quality complaints surged to 3 last week—a 2300% spike above the 0.1 weekly baseline—suggesting widespread HVAC failures, mold, or indoor contamination across residential or commercial buildings in this week or last week.
evidence: 3 indoor air quality complaints last week vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (2300% increase)
Z-score of 8.69 indicates extreme statistical anomaly
Timing coincides with winter heating season and potential building system failures
reporting_angles: Which buildings or neighborhoods are experiencing air quality problems—are they residential apartments, offices, or schools?
Are these complaints tied to specific causes: heating system failures, mold, or external pollution sources?

themes_detail.label: Street Obstruction Surge
themes_detail.summary: Obstruction complaints jumped to 14 last week, a 261% increase above the 3.9 weekly average, indicating widespread blockages of sidewalks or roadways that may impede pedestrian and vehicle traffic across CD 411.
evidence: 14 obstruction complaints last week vs. 3.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (261% increase)
Z-score of 8.68 indicates extreme statistical anomaly
Converges with spike in damaged street signs (5 this week vs. 1.8 avg)
reporting_angles: What types of obstructions are blocking streets and sidewalks—construction debris, illegally parked vehicles, or fallen trees?
Are obstructions concentrated in specific neighborhoods or commercial corridors?

themes_detail.label: Dead or Dying Trees Accelerating
themes_detail.summary: Dead or dying tree complaints rose to 15 last week, up 103% from the 7.4 weekly average, reflecting possible disease outbreak, inadequate maintenance, or winter stress affecting the urban canopy in this district.
evidence: 15 dead/dying tree complaints last week vs. 7.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (103% increase)
Z-score of 3.6 indicates significant statistical anomaly
Complements broader tree damage trend: 209 total damaged tree complaints over 90 days
reporting_angles: Is a specific tree disease or pest affecting CD 411, or is this attributable to winter damage and deferred maintenance?
How is Parks Department prioritizing removal and replanting in affected areas?

themes_detail.label: Unsanitary Conditions Jump
themes_detail.summary: Unsanitary condition complaints rose to 7 last week, a 93% spike above the 3.6 weekly average, suggesting accumulating trash, rodent activity, or other hygiene hazards in residential or commercial areas this week.
evidence: 7 unsanitary condition complaints last week vs. 3.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (93% increase)
Z-score of 2.77 indicates significant statistical anomaly
Converges with street/sidewalk noise complaints (9 last week vs. 4.8 avg), possibly indicating shared root cause in neglected public spaces
reporting_angles: Where are unsanitary conditions concentrated—specific streets, parks, or commercial corridors?
Is this tied to inadequate sanitation pickup, pest infestations, or illicit dumping?
